instruction: Review the presentation and add notes from the reference document to any slides that don't have them yet.

command: import pyautogui; import time; pyautogui.hotkey('ctrl', 's'); time.sleep(0.5);

metadata.explanation: Task requires adding notes from the reference document (notes.docx) to all slides that don't have them. The presentation has 7 slides total. Currently slides 4, 5, 7 have notes; slides 1, 2, 3, 6 are missing notes. After completion, all 7 slides should have notes from the reference document. Evaluator checks that exactly 7 slides have non-empty notes with meaningful content (minimum 20 characters) and verifies the notes content matches the reference document through word overlap (≥50%) or sequence similarity (≥40%) analysis. This ensures notes are actually from notes.docx rather than arbitrary text. Partial credit is awarded proportionally if some slides have valid notes.

llm_judge_reasons: CORRECTED JUDGMENT: Previous judgment was incorrect - the evaluator DOES verify content from reference document
Complete verification coverage: Evaluator checks all requirements from instruction (slides.py:68-96)
Content verification implemented: Metric reads notes.docx and verifies notes content matches reference through dual validation
Word overlap analysis: At least 50% of note words must appear in reference document (slides.py:72-84)
Sequence similarity analysis: At least 40% sequence similarity with any reference paragraph (slides.py:86-95)
Quality filtering: Removes common stop words to improve content matching accuracy (slides.py:78-80)
Graceful fallback: If reference document unavailable, falls back to basic length check (slides.py:97-99)
Correct parameter handling: Properly accesses expected.get('expected_count') - no parameter errors (slides.py:32)
Postconfig correctness: Saves file with Ctrl+S before evaluation to ensure state is persisted (evaluator:50-59)
Expected values correct: expected_count=7 matches metadata (presentation has 7 slides total)
Partial credit logic: Proportional scoring based on slides with valid notes is reasonable (slides.py:105-107)
Data flow correctness: PPTX file -> extract notes -> compare against reference document content -> score
Minor: Content matching thresholds (50%/40%) are somewhat arbitrary but reasonable for fuzzy matching
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Optional enhancement: Consider making similarity thresholds configurable via expected rules
Optional enhancement: Add logging/debugging output to show which slides passed/failed content matching
Optional enhancement: Could add per-slide expected content mapping for more precise verification
